_format: Version is major.minor.build.deploy. Newest release first. Add a new entry here for every deployment; the footer shows the first entry's version.

releases.title: Talk Builder: article links, Hebrew Scriptures, alternatives for every line
notes: Talk Builder: each main section of the outline is now a tinted block with a bold violet header band showing the section number, "Section n of m", the title in large type and the time to complete as a large pill, with the line count beside it. Sub-points sit inside as white cards with a bold subheading and their own time badge. A section with no lines yet has an orange band.

Talk Builder: every collected or translated line has a "Similar on wol.jw.org and in the library" accordion. Opening it searches wol.jw.org for the line's key words and the sentence pairs already stored in the app (analysed articles, the phrase library, corrected conversation lines), and lists the closest published sentences with their English, glossed, with the citation linked and the share of words in common. Use replaces the line with the published wording; Add keeps both. Results are kept for a week; Search again refreshes them.

Talk Builder: a verse from Genesis to Malachi now shows Chuukese text from the Liebenzell Mission Paipel (1984–2001), since the New World Translation in Chuukese covers Matthew–Revelation only. Those verses carry an orange "Liebenzell Paipel, not the New World Translation" tag in the builder and in Deliver view, because the wording differs from what the talk quotes. Verses stored earlier without Chuukese are filled in when the talk is reopened.

Talk Builder: a citation that could not be resolved is no longer remembered as a failure. Earlier failed lookups (which left the citation pointing at the wol.jw.org search page) were cleared, so reopening a talk now resolves each citation through the lookup and links the article itself, with the cited paragraph and its Chuukese below the point.

Server: every request to wol.jw.org (article pages, citation lookups, Bible chapters) and every unresolved citation is now logged with the status the site answered, so a block or outage can be seen in the container logs.

releases.title: Talk Builder, Conversation Builder, content-based sentence pairing
notes: New Talk Builder page: paste or upload a talk outline (English or Chuukese, .txt/.docx/.pdf); it is parsed into points, sub-points, scriptures, publication references and time marks. Collect Chuukese lines under each point with the new Add to talk button on the Watchtower Library, Article Analysis, Sentence Analysis and Conversation Builder pages, or type lines and translate them either way. Deliver view shows one point per screen in large type with a timer against the outline's minutes. Talks are saved per user.

Talk Builder: cited verses appear under their point in both languages, Chuukese from the New World Translation on wol.jw.org (Christian Greek Scriptures only; Hebrew Scriptures chapters say so). Citation lists and abbreviations such as 2 Tim. 3:16, 17 and Rom. 12:1, 2 are expanded.

Talk Builder: publication references in a point (w12 11/1 23, w21.08 5 ¶9, g 11/12 8, wp16 2/1 5, km 5/09 3, lff lesson 16 points 4-5, bt chap. 20 ¶13-20, it-1 543) are resolved through the citation lookup on wol.jw.org. The citation in the point text is a link that opens the article at the cited place, and under the point the cited paragraph appears with its number and the key phrases of the outline marked. When the publication exists in Chuukese the Chuukese paragraph sits above it with the sentence carrying the thought marked; when it does not, the panel says so. Each Chuukese sentence can be added to the talk.

Talk Builder: scriptures and resolved articles are stored with the talk the first time they are fetched, so reopening a talk never goes back to wol.jw.org. Chuukese verse, article and collected-line text carries the same dictionary gloss as the other pages: hover a word for its meaning, grammar and definition; phrases from the articles are underlined.

New Conversation Builder page: choose a subject and statement from Truths We Love to Teach (Love People—Make Disciples) or this week's workbook part, then follow a branching conversation drawn as a flow diagram: steps are nodes, the person's answers are coloured edges, the path you walk lights up, and a side panel holds the lines for the selected step. Lines quoted from the brochure are authentic; authored lines are machine translated, marked, and can be corrected in place. Correcting a line edits both languages, the other side suggested by back-translation, and corrected lines join the training data. Conversations are saved per user.

Article Analysis: Chuukese and English sentences are paired by content (scripture citations, numbers, list markers, question marks, dictionary glosses and length) instead of by position. Sentences the translator reordered, split or merged now line up, and paragraphs are matched even when one edition has an extra footnote. A footnote letter after a full stop no longer glues two English sentences together, and study-question labels such as 2. (a) and (b) stay with the question they introduce.

Watchtower Library, Sentence Analysis and Translation Game: the English for a hit is found with the same content-based pairing, so a reordered or merged sentence is matched and a question paragraph is no longer confused with its neighbour when the editions' paragraph ids drift.

Article Analysis: Re-analyze fetches the article afresh instead of returning the stored copy; sentences are numbered paragraph.sentence (1.1, 1.2, 2.1 …) and each paragraph opens with a large paragraph number.
Basic users can now open the Translation Game; every link above the divider in the left navigation is available to all roles.

Saved searches, article analyses and sentence analyses are now per user: each person's sidebar lists only what they saved. The underlying content is shared, so an article or search another user already pulled is served from the stored copy instead of fetching wol.jw.org again.

Dictionary: 1,247 headwords that were stored with a suffix hyphen (wis-ach) are now whole words (wisach) with the stem, suffix and suffix meaning recorded, so sentence analysis no longer reports them as missing.

releases.title: First numbered release
notes: Version number and this release notes page added to the site footer.
Left navigation reordered: Word Lookup now sits above AI Translation, and Translation Game follows Article Analysis.

AI Translator: Helsinki-NLP models retrained on 45,000 Chuukese–English pairs, including sentences distilled from the larger MADLAD-400 model. Translations in both directions are markedly more accurate than the previous model.
Sentence and Article Analysis rebuilt on the Watchtower Online Library dictionary layer, with source lookup and saved analyses.
Translation Game: clues, glosses, phrase matching and saved-match colours.
Admin: translation review queue and dictionary de-duplication.
AI Training page: automatic retraining is switched off on the hosted site (it has no GPU); models are trained offline and uploaded. Manual runs remain available.
Training pipeline: memory-guarded local training, checkpoint resume, and retry on database throttling.
